## Alternatives considered

**Recycle `SEEN` cards too, once the deferred pile is also drained.** The literal
reading of "repeat them all once the difficulty is finished", and rejected for now.
`SEEN` is load-bearing for the 80% gate and `UserSubtopicProgress.seen_count`;
returning those cards to rotation means either double-counting coverage or teaching
every counter to ignore repeats. Since a scroller marks almost nothing `SEEN`, the
deferred pile alone already delivers the endless feed. Revisit if readers who
*do* read start hitting the wall.

**Mark a card consumed the moment it is served, in `build_slate`.** Simplest possible
rule and no client change. Rejected: serving is not seeing. A card at the bottom of a
page the reader never scrolls to would be burned unseen, and the reader would never
know what they missed.

**Advance the cycle from a batch job**, as the old test's comment imagined. Rejected:
it puts a user-visible latency between "ran out" and "has more", for a decision that
is one `EXISTS` query on a path already known to be empty. Nothing about it needs to
be asynchronous.

**Key the difficulty-mix ramp off cards shown rather than cards read.** Considered
and deliberately not done. `dynamic_mix` holds a reader at 100% of their own tier
until they have read 20% of it, so a scroller never sees the 20% intermediate slice.
Loosening that would hand people harder cards they have no grounding in, which is the
ramp's entire purpose — and since tier promotion requires passing a quiz, a scroller
stays at their tier regardless. Left alone until the simpler fix has been felt.

## Revisit when

- Readers who actually read report running out. That is the signal the `SEEN`
  alternative above is now worth its complexity.
- The 1000ms impression threshold is measured against real scroll behaviour rather
  than assumed. Either failure mode showing up in engagement data should move it.
- `FeedPage.starved` gains a consumer. It currently has none — the router drops it
  and no fill job is enqueued from a starved read, so ADR-0006's demand-driven fill
  loop is only half-wired. Recycling keeps the feed moving over a corpus that is too
  small, which makes that gap easier to ignore and more important to close.

adrs.title: ADR-0051: A "no color" opt-out for per-topic accent, via a sentinel hue
adrs.summary: Adding a third accent state so a topic can opt out of color tinting entirely, alongside the deterministic-default and chosen-hue states.
adrs.content:
# ADR-0051: A "no color" opt-out for per-topic accent, via a sentinel hue

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-08-22
- **Deciders:** Anubhav
- **Amends:** [ADR-0034](/work/spoin#adr-0034) -- `UserTopic.accent_hue`
  gains a third meaning for the same column; no new field.

## Context

ADR-0034 gave `UserTopic.accent_hue` two states: `null` ("use the deterministic
default hue") and `0-359` ("use this hue"). Every topic renders tinted, one way or
another -- there was no way to say "don't tint this topic at all, just use the
palette's own accent," which is exactly what `--topic-accent` already falls back to
whenever a card sets no `--topic-hue` (`globals.css`'s `--topic-accent: var(--accent)`
base case). That fallback already existed structurally; nothing exposed it as a user
choice.

The request is a "no color" option in the existing swatch picker (`TopicStatsModal`)
that lands on this fallback deliberately, for users who find per-topic tinting noisy
in a mixed feed or simply prefer every card to read as "this palette," unmodified.

## Decision

**A third state on the same `accent_hue` column, via the sentinel `-1` --
`NO_TOPIC_COLOR` in `lib/topicColor.ts`.** No migration: the column is already a plain
nullable `Integer` with no `CHECK` constraint, so a third meaning costs nothing on the
schema. `TopicColorIn.hue`'s validator widens from `ge=0` to `ge=-1`.

**All three states, spelled out:**

| `accent_hue` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `null` | Use the deterministic default hue (ADR-0034) |
| `0-359` | Use this hue |
| `-1` (`NO_TOPIC_COLOR`) | Opt out -- render the palette's plain `--accent`, no `--topic-hue` set |

**`topicHue()` is the only place that interprets the sentinel.** It now returns
`number | null` instead of a bare `number`: `null` means "set no `--topic-hue`," which
every consumer already needs to handle correctly (Card.tsx's expanded border, hero
ring, `.card-topic`, saved tiles) since that's the same shape `--topic-accent`'s CSS
fallback already expects. Three call sites (`SavedView`, `LikedView`, `NotesView`'s
collection-filter chips) were reading `UserTopic.accent_hue` directly off the wire
instead of through `topicHue()` -- those are the ones a sentinel would silently break,
rendering `-1` as a red-ish hue via `oklch(from var(--accent) l c -1deg)` instead of no
color at all. They're moved onto a new `explicitTopicHue()`, which was already their
actual intent (tint only on an explicitly chosen hue, never the computed default) --
the opt-out state and "never colored, no default shown" were already indistinguishable
there before this change, and stay that way, which is correct for a chip meant to
label an actively-chosen color.

**No new picker widget.** The existing 8-swatch row in `TopicStatsModal` (ADR-0034's
"discrete swatches, not a continuous wheel" pattern) gains a 9th control: filled with
the plain `--accent` (honest -- that's exactly what selecting it renders) with a
diagonal slash overlay, the conventional "no fill" affordance distinguishing it from a
hue choice rather than looking like one more color.

## Consequences

**Easier**
- Zero schema changes; the whole feature is a validator range widen, a client-side
  sentinel constant, and a picker button.
- A user who finds mixed-feed tinting noisy can turn it off per topic without losing
  the ability to turn it back on (still stores a real value, just a specific one).

**Harder**
- `accent_hue`'s three-state meaning now lives only in code comments and this ADR, not
  in the type system -- `number | null` on the wire doesn't distinguish "a hue" from
  "the opt-out sentinel." A reviewer unfamiliar with this ADR could reasonably read
  `-1` as a bug. Mitigated by requiring every read to route through `topicHue()`/
  `explicitTopicHue()` rather than reading `accent_hue` raw, with a comment on the
  field pointing here.

## Alternatives considered

**A second boolean column (`color_enabled` or similar).** Rejected: makes the pair a
two-column invariant (a `hue` alongside an `enabled` that can disagree) for a state
that fits in the existing nullable int's unused negative range, and would have needed
a migration `set_color` and every reader don't otherwise need.

**Redefine `null` as "no color" and always materialize a real hue at subscribe time.**
The cleanest data model in isolation, but it inverts ADR-0034's whole point --
`null`'s value *is* "compute the default lazily, no write needed just to have one."
Redefining it would also mean a backfill `UPDATE` across every existing `UserTopic`
row in `spoin_db`, which CLAUDE.md gates behind the project owner's explicit approval
even framed as routine maintenance. Rejected without asking, since the sentinel
achieves the same user-facing result with no data migration at all.

## Revisit when

If a topic-level (not per-user) "no color" default is ever wanted -- e.g. an
editorially flagged topic that should never tint regardless of who's viewing --
that's a `Topic`-level field the same way ADR-0034's "Revisit when" describes for a
shared accent color, with `UserTopic.accent_hue` still taking precedence when set
(including the sentinel).

adrs.title: ADR-0052: A single-slot undo toast for removal in Notes/Liked/Saved
adrs.summary: A 5-second undo toast for removing notes, likes, and bookmarks, plus a cross-view store fixing stale liked/bookmarked state.
adrs.content:
# ADR-0052: A single-slot undo toast for removal in Notes/Liked/Saved

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-08-22
- **Deciders:** Anubhav

## Context

Removing a card from Notes, Liked, or Saved was already a one-click, no-confirmation
action -- consistent with those views' optimistic-update pattern (unlike/unbookmark/
delete-note all update local state immediately, before the server round-trip
resolves). Nothing softened an accidental removal. The request is an undo affordance:
a bottom toast, live for 5 seconds, dismissible early via an X.

Two things make this more than "add a toast":

1. **The three "remove" actions are not the same operation.** Unliking and
   unbookmarking are hard `DELETE`s of `CardLike`/`CardBookmark` rows
   ([engagement/service.py](../../apps/api/src/spoin/engagement/service.py)).
   Deleting a note is `DELETE /cards/{id}/note`. There is no shared "soft delete" or
   "trash" concept anywhere in this schema to lean on (CLAUDE.md is explicit that
   `spoin_db` has none, and inventing one for this alone would be a parallel
   mechanism for a five-second convenience).
2. **Every collection view stays mounted-but-hidden once visited**
   (`AppShell`'s `visited` set, `hidden` attribute, never unmounted) so switching
   from Liked to Notes mid-countdown must not lose the toast. A toast owned by the
   view that triggered it would disappear the moment its subtree goes `hidden`.

## Decision

**Delete immediately; undo re-creates, it does not un-delete.** Each view captures
the full row it's about to drop from its own already-in-memory `rows` state, filters
it out (unchanged optimistic-update behavior), and hands the captured row to
`offerUndo()`. Undo re-issues the *original* mutating call -- `engagement.record(id,
"like")`, `engagement.record(id, "bookmark")`, or `api.saveNote(id, body)` -- and
re-inserts the row into local state. No new "pending delete" state, no deferred
write: the row is genuinely gone and genuinely restorable, the same way a real user
action would redo it.

**The honest cost this accepts: undo is a fresh row, not a reversal.** A re-liked
card gets a new `CardLike.created_at`; a restored note gets a new `updated_at`. Both
surface in "RECENT" sort order jumping the item to the top. This was chosen over
inventing soft-delete specifically to avoid a second schema concept for a UI
convenience -- see Alternatives.

**One undo slot, newest wins -- `lib/undo.ts`, a module-level store mirroring
`lib/refresh.ts`'s pub/sub shape** (this codebase's existing pattern for
"one piece of client state several disconnected components need to see and react
to"). `offerUndo()` replaces whatever offer is currently live and restarts its
5-second timer; there is no queue. Removing a second card while the first's toast is
still showing makes the first item permanently gone -- deliberately, matching how
Gmail's archive/delete toast behaves, rather than turning a lightweight affordance
into a list the user has to triage.

**One toast component, mounted once in `AppShell`, outside every view's subtree.**
`UndoToast` subscribes to the store and renders fixed-position, bottom-center,
`z-index: 120` (above the Saved-card overlay's `z-index: 100`, below the custom
cursor's `999`). This is what makes "switch views mid-countdown, toast survives"
work at all -- a toast rendered inside `LikedView`'s own tree would vanish under
`hidden` the instant the user navigates away.

**The X dismisses; it does not undo.** Clicking it calls `dismissUndo()`, which
clears the timer and the slot -- the removal already happened and stays that way.
This is worth stating because "X" on a toast is occasionally misread as "cancel the
action" rather than "stop offering to reverse it."

**`role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"`, not a focus-stealing dialog.** The toast
announces itself to assistive tech without interrupting whatever the user is doing,
consistent with how `GuestNotice` (the only other standing toast-like surface) is
built.

## Consequences

**Easier**
- Every "remove" action across the three views gets undo with the same ~15-line
  shape: capture row → filter → `offerUndo`. No new API endpoints, no schema
  changes.
- The store is view-agnostic; extending undo to the feed's like/bookmark toggle or
  to unfollowing a topic later is a call to `offerUndo`, not new infrastructure.

**Harder**
- `accent_hue`-style "one true value" reasoning doesn't apply here: the event log
  now honestly contains like → unlike → like sequences from a single accidental tap
  + undo, which is correct under ADR-0011's event/state/aggregate separation but is
  a fact worth knowing before reading engagement events as literal user intent.
- A 5-second window is short for a screen-reader or keyboard user to react to a live
  region and act before it disappears (WCAG 2.2.1 is stricter than this). Accepted
  because the removal is already committed -- the timeout only withdraws a
  convenience, it never destroys data outright, and the requested behavior was
  explicit about the 5-second figure.
- Restoring a row inserts it at the front of the client's in-memory list rather than
  recomputing where the active sort (`recent`/`oldest`/`topic`/`difficulty`) would
  actually place it -- all three sorts are server-side (`api.likedCards`/
  `savedCards`/`listNotes` take the sort key), so an exact client-side re-sort would
  duplicate that logic. The next natural refetch (the same `invalidate()` call each
  original removal already triggers) corrects the position.

## Alternatives considered

**A real soft-delete / trash table**, restorable without a new write. Rejected:
introduces a schema concept (`deleted_at` or a trash table) that nothing else in
this codebase has, for a five-second UI convenience -- the kind of thing CLAUDE.md's
"anything that must be *true* is enforced outside the model" framing would call
over-engineering in the other direction: adding a durable mechanism for a transient
UI state.

**Deferring the actual `DELETE`/`unlike` call until the 5 seconds elapse**, so undo
is simply "never send it." Rejected: `unlike`/`unbookmark` are in
`engagement.ts`'s `URGENT` set specifically because progression-adjacent state
should not sit unflushed client-side; a 5-second hold before *any* write would
invert that guarantee, and the row would need to be faked as already-removed in the
UI regardless, so nothing about this decision gets simpler.

**A toast queue** instead of a single replaced slot. Rejected: turns "quick
convenience if you misclick" into a small triage UI for anyone removing several
things in a row, which is the more common case (batch-cleaning Saved) this feature
is least useful for anyway.

## Revisit when

- If undo is wanted for the feed's own like/bookmark toggle, or for unfollowing a
  topic, `offerUndo`/`UndoToast` already generalize -- no redesign needed, just a
  new call site.
- If the 5-second window turns out to be a real accessibility complaint in practice
  (not hypothetical), lengthen it or pause the timer on focus/hover before reaching
  for a queue or a differently-shaped affordance.

docs.title: Continuum System Architecture: Event-Sourced Directed Multigraph
docs.summary: Production continuity engine treating a film as an immutable event ledger in ClickHouse with multi-agent orchestration via Vertex AI.
docs.content:
# Technical Architecture: Continuum (The AI-Native Studio OS) **Hackathon:** Agentic Cinema: The Blockbuster Hackathon (Google Cloud) **Primary Partner:** ClickHouse Cloud (`mcp-clickhouse` & HTTP Streamable API) **Core Frameworks:** Google Cloud Agent Builder (ADK), Gemini Enterprise, FastMCP / Model Context Protocol **Repository:** [github.com/anubhav-qt/continuum](https://github.com/anubhav-qt/continuum) --- ## 1. Architectural Philosophy & Core Tenets 1. **State ≠ Agent (Ground Truth Separation):** The movie is not a prompt context window; it is an **explicit, queryable, and immutable State Graph** persisted in ClickHouse. Agents reason over, traverse, and propose changes to this ground truth rather than hallucinating it. 2. **Cyclic Directed Graph with Cycle Controls:** Film production is inherently cyclic (e.g. on-set actor limitations or flashback changes loop back upstream into the script, which propagates back downstream into call sheets and permits). The graph is modeled as a **Directed Cyclic Multigraph** with cycle-breaking convergence algorithms and human escalation gates. 3. **Event-Sourced Immutability:** Every single prompt, human edit, agent impact proposal, approval, rejection, and task dispatch is an immutable event logged in ClickHouse. 4. **Role-Sliced Projections (Zero Noise):** Crew members (Actors, Costume Designers, Gaffers, Line Producers) only query their craft-specific slice of the production state graph. 5. **Deterministic Invariants over Stochastic LLM Guarantees:** Constraints like budget limits, schedule deadlines, and recursion depth are strictly enforced in deterministic application code and ClickHouse queries, never solely delegated to model system instructions. --- ## 2. Costume, Lighting, Stunts, Sound] end subgraph ORCH_LAYER["Vertex AI Agent Builder — Multi-Agent Orchestration"] MASTER[🤖 Studio Master Orchestrator Agent

Slices state into role-filtered directives] A_QC[🔍 8. QC & Verification Agent
Plan-vs-output multimodal diffing] end subgraph MCP_DATA_PLANE["Model Context Protocol (MCP) & ClickHouse Engine"] CH_MCP[⚡ ClickHouse MCP Server
`mcp-clickhouse` & Client] CH_DB[(ClickHouse Cloud
Event Ledger, State Nodes, Edges, Role Directives)] GCP_DOCS[📑 Vertex AI Search & Multimodal Tools] end UI_LAYER <--> MASTER MASTER --> SPECIALIZED_AGENTS SPECIALIZED_AGENTS <--> CH_MCP SPECIALIZED_AGENTS <--> GCP_DOCS CH_MCP <--> CH_DB ``` --- ## 3. Data Model & ClickHouse Event Schema ### 3.1 `production_events` (Append-Only Event Sourcing) Stores the entire immutable audit trail of the studio. ```sql CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS production_events ( event_id UUID DEFAULT generateUUIDv4(), project_id UUID, revision_id UInt64, cascade_session_id Nullable(UUID), -- Groups multi-epoch cascade passes epoch_index UInt8 DEFAULT 0, -- 0 = root trigger, 1 = pass 1, 2 = pass 2 timestamp DateTime64(6) DEFAULT now64(6), actor_role LowCardinality(String), -- 'DIRECTOR', 'PRODUCER', 'WRITER', 'AGENT_CONTINUITY', etc. actor_id String, -- User identifier or Agent name event_type LowCardinality(String), -- 'NODE_UPDATED', 'PROPOSAL_GENERATED', 'PROPOSAL_REJECTED', 'REVISION_COMMITTED' node_id Nullable(String), payload_json String, -- Strongly-typed JSON payload diff_json String -- JSON diff: { "before": {...}, "after": {...} } ) ENGINE = MergeTree() PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(timestamp) ORDER BY (project_id, revision_id, timestamp, event_id); ``` ### 3.2 `graph_nodes` (Current & Historical Entity State) Represents film entities (Scenes, Characters, Props, Locations, Shots, Call Sheets, Budget Items). ```sql CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS graph_nodes ( project_id UUID, node_id String, -- e.g. 'scene_12', 'char_arjun', 'shot_12_a' revision_id UInt64, stage LowCardinality(String), -- 'PREMISE', 'SCRIPT', 'SCREENPLAY', 'LOGISTICS', 'DIRECTOR_SHOTS', 'CREW_DIRECTIVES', 'QC' node_type LowCardinality(String), -- 'SCENE', 'CHARACTER', 'PROP', 'LOCATION', 'SHOT', 'RESOURCE', 'DIRECTIVE', 'QC_ASSERTION' title String, content_json String, -- Validated Pydantic JSON payload content_hash String, -- SHA-256 for O(1) differential change detection & loop quenching status LowCardinality(String), -- 'ACTIVE', 'STALE', 'PROPOSED', 'SUPERSEDED', 'CONFLICT' embedding Array(Float32), -- Vector embedding for semantic search author_role LowCardinality(String), created_at DateTime64(3) DEFAULT now64(3), updated_at DateTime64(3) DEFAULT now64(3) ) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at) ORDER BY (project_id, node_id, revision_id); ``` ### 3.3 `graph_edges` (Cyclic Dependency Graph) Defines upstream and downstream links with explicit invalidation rules. ```sql CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS graph_edges ( project_id UUID, edge_id UUID DEFAULT generateUUIDv4(), from_node_id String, -- Parent / Upstream node (e.g. 'scene_12') to_node_id String, -- Dependent node (e.g. 'shot_12_a', 'call_sheet_day_4') edge_type LowCardinality(String), -- 'NARRATIVE_FLOW', 'PROP_USAGE', 'LOCATION_USAGE', 'CHARACTER_PRESENCE', 'BUDGET_LINK' invalidation_rule LowCardinality(String), -- 'HARD_STALE', 'SOFT_WARNING', 'REVERIFY_ONLY' created_at DateTime64(3) DEFAULT now64(3) ) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY (project_id, from_node_id, to_node_id, edge_id); ``` ### 3.4 `proposals` (Impact Analysis & Negotiation Ledger) Tracks the proposal lifecycle and multi-stakeholder negotiation logs. ```sql CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS proposals ( proposal_id UUID DEFAULT generateUUIDv4(), project_id UUID, trigger_node_id String, proposed_by_role LowCardinality(String), status LowCardinality(String), -- 'PENDING_REVIEW', 'APPROVED', 'REJECTED', 'NEGOTIATING', 'COMMITTED' summary String, impact_json String, -- { budget_delta: 4200, schedule_drift_days: 1, affected_nodes: [...], affected_roles: [...] } negotiation_history String, -- Structured chat logs & compromise alternatives created_at DateTime64(3) DEFAULT now64(3), resolved_at Nullable(DateTime64(3)) ) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(created_at) ORDER BY (project_id, proposal_id); ``` ### 3.5 `role_directives` (Craft-Filtered Slices) Serves materialized, noise-free task views for crew members. ```sql CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS role_directives ( directive_id UUID DEFAULT generateUUIDv4(), project_id UUID, revision_id UInt64, target_role LowCardinality(String),-- 'ACTOR', 'COSTUME_MAKEUP', 'LIGHTING_CAMERA', 'STUNT_CHOREO', 'SOUND_MUSIC', 'PRODUCER', 'DIRECTOR' target_person_id Nullable(String), -- Specific actor/crew member ID scene_id Nullable(String), priority LowCardinality(String), -- 'CRITICAL', 'HIGH', 'NORMAL' headline String, instruction_markdown String, status LowCardinality(String), -- 'PENDING', 'ACKNOWLEDGED', 'COMPLETED' created_at DateTime64(3) DEFAULT now64(3) ) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(created_at) ORDER BY (project_id, target_role, revision_id, directive_id); ``` --- ## 4. Multi-Agent & MCP Tooling Strategy ### 4.1 Specialized Agents & Model Strategy *All LLM model assignments are marked as **TBD** and will be benchmarked per agent during implementation.* | Agent Name | Model Tier | Core Responsibility | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Discovery & Ingestion Agent** | `TBD` | Unbiased discovery interviews & multimodal script PDF/FDX parsing | | **Story & Screenplay Agent** | `TBD` | Narrative beat drafting, scene structuring, dialogue writing | | **Pre-Production Logistics Agent** | `TBD` | Budget calculation, call-sheet generation, permit verification | | **Director & Shot Agent** | `TBD` | Camera blocking, coverage angles, visual pacing, lens selection | | **Continuity & Invalidation Agent** | `TBD` | Blast radius calculation, physical/temporal invariant assertions | | **Negotiation & Brainstorming Agent** | `TBD` | Collaborative multi-stakeholder negotiation & compromise solver | | **Role Dispatch Agent** | `TBD` | Translation of global graph diffs into craft-sliced directives | | **QC & Verification Agent** | `TBD` | Plan-vs-output multimodal diffing against ground truth | ### 4.2 ClickHouse MCP Tool Definitions Agents interact with the data layer via typed MCP tools: 1. `query_graph_nodes(project_id, revision_id, stage, node_type)` 2. `get_blast_radius(project_id, modified_node_id, direction)` 3. `record_production_event(project_id, actor_role, event_type, payload, diff)` 4. `dispatch_role_directives(project_id, revision_id, directives_list)` 5. `search_semantic_nodes(project_id, query_embedding, top_k)` ## 5. Bi-Directional Cascade & Invalidation Engine The cascade engine propagates mutations across the cyclic production graph using a **Fixed-Point Iterative Relaxation** algorithm. It guarantees that multi-pass circular dependencies either converge to a stable state or safely halt for human escalation. ```mermaid graph TD A[Trigger Change on Node X] --> B[Epoch 1: Compute 1-Hop Blast Radius in ClickHouse] B --> C[Mark 1-Hop Dependent Nodes as STALE] C --> D[Specialized Domain Agents Re-derive Stale Nodes] D --> E{Content Hash Check:
Did new JSON hash differ from old?} E -->|Hash Unchanged| F[Branch Converged & Pruned] E -->|Hash Changed| G[Queue Next 1-Hop Dependents] G --> H{Oscillation & Epoch Limit Check} H -->|State Signature Repeated: Oscillation Detected| ESC[🚨 Stop & Escalate to Human:
Circular conflict detected] H -->|Epoch Index >= max_epochs (3)| ESC H -->|Epoch Index < 3 & Active Changes Exist| B F --> CONV[State Converged & Consistent] CONV --> PACK[Generate Impact Proposal Pack] ESC --> PACK ``` --- ### 5.1 Invalidation Rules & Edge Invariant Types | Edge Type | Example Dependency | Invalidation Rule | Invalidation Behavior | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **`NARRATIVE_FLOW`** | Scene 4 $\rightarrow$ Scene 5 | `SOFT_WARNING` | Flagged for Scriptwriter; re-runs dialogue continuity pass. | | **`LOCATION_USAGE`** | Scene 4 $\rightarrow$ Logistics Day 2 | `HARD_STALE` | Marks location permit, booking fee, and travel schedule STALE. | | **`PROP_USAGE`** | Scene 4 $\rightarrow$ Prop "Golden Watch" | `HARD_STALE` | Marks prop chain in subsequent scenes STALE. | | **`CHARACTER_PRESENCE`** | Scene 4 $\rightarrow$ Call Sheet Day 2 | `HARD_STALE` | Re-derives cast call times, hair/makeup slots, and wardrobe needs. | | **`CONTINUITY_INVARIANT`** | Arjun Wound $\rightarrow$ Scene 8 | `HARD_STALE` | Continuity agent asserts visual wound/bandage presence in Scene 8. | --- ### 5.2 Mathematical Bounds & Loop Prevention 1. **1-Hop Bounded Expansion:** ClickHouse MCP `get_blast_radius` performs strictly bounded 1-hop (or max 2-hop) queries per epoch rather than unbounded graph recursion. 2. **Differential Content Hashing (`content_hash`):** Nodes store a SHA-256 hash of their normalized JSON payload. If an agent re-evaluates a node and computes the identical output, propagation along that branch **immediately stops (quenches)**. 3. **Sub-Graph Oscillation Detector:** The engine computes a `subgraph_state_signature` (hash of all active node hashes in the current epoch). If this signature matches a signature from a previous epoch, an oscillation (ping-pong loop) is detected and immediately halted. 4. **Hard Epoch Ceiling (`max_cascade_epochs = 3`):** Any cascade reaching 3 passes without complete convergence is automatically halted and surfaced to the human producer/director with the exact conflicting cycle trace. --- ### 5.3 Strongly-Typed Impact Proposal Pack Schema When a cascade completes (or halts for escalation), it produces an `ImpactProposalPack` (Pydantic model): ```json { "proposal_id": "prop_9a12bc", "cascade_session_id": "7b0b68a3-2c1a-4d92-8f92-ec812a4b3d11", "trigger_node_id": "scene_4", "author_role": "DIRECTOR", "summary": "Location updated from Sunny Park to Night Warehouse", "epochs_executed": 2, "converged": true, "deltas": { "budget_delta": 4200.00, "schedule_drift_days": 1, "stale_nodes_count": 6, "affected_roles": ["PRODUCER", "COSTUME_MAKEUP", "LIGHTING_CAMERA", "ACTOR"] }, "role_impact_breakdown": { "PRODUCER": "Requires $4,200 additional budget for night lighting and wet set cleaning.", "COSTUME_MAKEUP": "3 duplicate wet wardrobe shirts required for Character Arjun.", "LIGHTING_CAMERA": "Switching to 5600K night rain lighting package.", "ACTOR": "Call time shifted from 08:00 AM to 07:00 PM for Character Arjun." }, "conflicts": [], "status": "PENDING_REVIEW" } ``` ## 6. Collaborative Negotiation & Brainstorming State Machine When a human rejects or contests an impact proposal, the system activates the **Collaborative Negotiation State Machine**, moving from static evaluation to active, constraint-satisfying mediation. ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> ProposalPending: Impact Proposal Generated ProposalPending --> Approved: Producer & Director Sign Off Approved --> Dispatched: Commit Revision to ClickHouse & Dispatch Tasks ProposalPending --> NegotiationActive: Rejection / Conflict Triggered state NegotiationActive { [*] --> ConstraintExtraction: Parse Human Objection (e.g. "Max $2k budget") ConstraintExtraction --> GenerateAlternatives: Brainstorming Agent Formulates 2-3 Creative Options GenerateAlternatives --> MultiStakeholderChat: Present Options in Collaborative UI MultiStakeholderChat --> CoEditOption: Humans pick or refine an option CoEditOption --> RevalidateConstraints: Agent runs mini-cascade on chosen option RevalidateConstraints --> OptionAgreed: Consensus Reached } NegotiationActive --> ProposalPending: Re-submit as Refined Proposal NegotiationActive --> Abandoned: Humans Cancel Proposal Dispatched --> [*] Abandoned --> [*] ``` --- ### 6.1 The 4 Capabilities of the Negotiation Agent 1. **Constraint Extraction:** Parses natural language objections into hard and soft constraints (e.g., *"We only have $2,500 left in contingency and Actor Arjun cannot shoot past 10 PM"*). 2. **Alternative Synthesis (Creative Compromise Engine):** Formulates 2 to 3 viable compromise plans that respect extracted constraints: * **Alternative A (Budget-Optimized):** Replaces physical rain with day-for-night VFX grading (Saves $2,400, adds 1 VFX task). * **Alternative B (Schedule-Optimized):** Shifts scene to an interior soundstage set (Zero weather risk, costs +$1,800). * **Alternative C (Script-Optimized):** Keeps original day park location, but alters dialogue to reflect tension through background audio ambiance. 3. **Multi-Stakeholder Consensus Tracking:** Tracks approvals from both the **Producer** (budget/logistics sign-off) and **Director** (creative vision sign-off). 4. **Negotiation Audit Log:** Every chat message, proposed alternative, and user rationale is serialized into the `proposals` table in ClickHouse under `negotiation_history`. --- ### 6.2 Pydantic Schema for Negotiation ```python class NegotiationAlternative(BaseModel): alternative_id: str title: str rationale: str budget_delta: float schedule_drift_days: int modified_node_payloads: dict[str, Any] department_impacts: dict[str, str] tradeoffs: list[str] class NegotiationSession(BaseModel): proposal_id: str objection_summary: str extracted_constraints: list[str] active_alternatives: list[NegotiationAlternative] status: Literal["NEGOTIATING", "CONSENSUS_REACHED", "ABANDONED"] ``` ## 7. Control Center Frontend Architecture & Role Portals (v1 Baseline) > [!NOTE] > **Iterative UI Evolution Notice:** This section specifies the **v1 baseline** for the frontend control center. While backend state and graph semantics remain strictly bounded, the user interface and interaction patterns will be continuously iterated and refined based on visual feedback, usability testing, and demo recording requirements. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph FRONTEND["Web Workspace (React / Next.js / TypeScript)"] NAV[Top Navigation: Project Selector, Revision Timeline Slider, Persona Role Switcher] subgraph MAIN_CANVAS["Dynamic Center Canvas (Persona-Dependent)"] GRAPH_VIEW[📊 Interactive State Graph Visualizer
React Flow / Canvas with live cascade node animations] DIFF_VIEW[📑 Side-by-Side Impact & Revision Diff Viewer] ROLE_PORTAL[🎭 Sliced Role Portal
Actor lines, Costume sheet, Lighting rig, Producer budget] QC_VIEW[🔍 QC Verification Dashboard
Video player with node-linked violation pins] end subgraph RIGHT_PANEL["Agent & Collaboration Stream"] EVENT_STREAM[⚡ Live ClickHouse Event Stream & Epoch Activity] BRAINSTORM_CHAT[🤝 Multi-Stakeholder Brainstorming Drawer] end end subgraph BACKEND_API["Backend API Layer (CQRS Read Path)"] API[API Endpoints: /api/v1/graph, /api/v1/directives, /api/v1/proposals] end NAV --> MAIN_CANVAS MAIN_CANVAS <--> API RIGHT_PANEL <--> API ``` --- ### 7.1 The 4 Core UI Views 1. **View 1: The Production Graph & Live Cascade Visualizer (The Hero View)** * Interactive node-link canvas rendering all movie entities (Story Beats, Scenes, Characters, Props, Call Sheets, Budget Items). * Visual state animations: * Direct 1-hop dependents flash **Amber / Stale**. * Re-deriving agents pulse with active indicator. * Successfully converged nodes glow **Green / Active**. * Circular conflicts pulse in **Crimson / Conflict**. 2. **View 2: Multi-Persona Role Switcher (Zero-Noise Slicing)** * **Producer:** Budget burn charts, permit tracking, critical path schedule, proposal sign-off queue. * **Director:** Scene mood boards, camera coverage, shot lists, lens choices, pacing curves. * **Writer:** Screenplay editor, character arcs, dialogue consistency diffs. * **Actor (e.g. Lead "Arjun"):** Character emotional arc, personal call times, exact dialogue lines, physical continuity badges (*"Left hand bandaged"*). * **Craft Departments (Costume, Lighting, Stunts, Sound):** Clean, checklist-style actionable cards with zero script noise. 3. **View 3: Collaborative Brainstorming & Proposal Drawer** * Side-by-side diff inspector showing precise before/after entity changes. * Impact metric chips: Budget delta, schedule drift, affected departments. * Real-time multi-stakeholder chat with the **Negotiation Agent** to review compromise alternatives. 4. **View 4: Plan-vs-Output QC Verification Dashboard** * Multimodal video/audio player with timestamped violation markers. * Direct node traceability: clicking any error highlights the exact `graph_node` and screenplay text it violated. --- ### 7.2 Frontend Technical Stack & Design System * **Framework:** React / Next.js with TypeScript (Strict mode). * **Graph Engine:** `@xyflow/react` / `reactflow` with custom SVG nodes for smooth 60fps pan/zoom. * **Design Theme:** Sleek, dark-mode cinematic studio theme (deep obsidian `#0D0E15`, accent cyan `#00F0FF`, status amber `#FFB800`, success emerald `#00E599`). * **Real-Time Communication:** Server-Sent Events (SSE) / WebSockets for streaming agent cascade epochs and negotiation chat messages. * **API Client:** Single typed API client (`lib/api.ts`) generated from the OpenAPI schema.

# Product Specification: Continuum (The AI-Native Studio OS) **Hackathon Track:** Google Cloud — Agentic Cinema: The Blockbuster Hackathon **Partner Integration:** ClickHouse (State & Event Sourcing Backbone via `mcp-clickhouse`) **AI Platform:** Google Cloud Agent Builder & Gemini Enterprise --- ## 1. Product Vision & Value Proposition > **Continuum** is an AI-native virtual film studio operating system that coordinates the entire lifecycle of movie production—from initial concept or document ingestion to final quality control. Instead of a generic prompt-to-video generator, Continuum is a **collaborative, multi-agent production orchestration platform**. It treats a film not as disconnected text documents, but as an **interconnected, persistent, and verifiable Production State Graph**. ### Core Value Pillars 1. **Frictionless Onboarding:** Start from scratch via unbiased interactive discovery, or import existing screenplays and production documents (PDFs/DOCs) at any stage. 2. **Role-Tailored Perspectives:** Every department (Producer, Director, Writer, Actor, Costume/Makeup, Stunts, Lighting, Sound) sees only the precise information, tasks, and alerts relevant to their craft. 3. **Bi-Directional Change Cascade:** Changes made at any stage automatically propagate upstream and downstream, triggering impact analysis across budget, schedule, shot lists, and call sheets. 4. **Collaborative Brainstorming & Negotiation:** If a proposed change is rejected or causes conflicts, specialized agents enter collaborative negotiation to suggest creative alternatives that satisfy real-world constraints. 5. **Deterministic Continuity Backbone:** The movie's ground truth (character states, prop locations, timeline consistency, dialogue accuracy) is tracked deterministically and verified against production outputs. --- ## 2. User Personas & Role-Scoped Views Every crew member interacts with Continuum through a persona-tailored workspace: ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ CONTINUUM OS │ ├───────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┤ │ ROLE │ PRIMARY FOCUS │ TAILORED VIEW CONTENT │ ├───────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ │ 💼 Producer │ Budget, Schedule, Logistics │ Cost burn rate, permit │ │ │ & Risk Management │ status, critical paths │ ├───────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ │ 🎬 Director │ Creative Vision, Camera │ Scene mood, pacing, │ │ │ Blocking, Shot Execution │ shot lists, coverage │ ├───────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ │ ✍️ Writer │ Dialogue, Narrative Beats, │ Screenplay editor, │ │ │ Scene Structure │ character arcs, diffs │ ├───────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ │ 🎭 Actor │ Performance, Lines, Calls │ Personal call sheets, │ │ │ & Character Continuity │ cues, physical state │ ├───────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ │ 🎨 Department │ Specialized Craft Execution │ Sliced work orders │ │ Crew │ (Wardrobe, Stunts, Lighting) │ with zero script noise │ └───────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘ ``` ### Department-Specific Breakdown: * **Costume & Makeup:** Tracks character injury states, wardrobe continuity across non-linear shoot days, prosthetic requirements. * **Lighting & Cinematography:** Gaffer/DP setups, color temperatures, day-for-night profiles, camera gear packages. * **Stunts & Choreography:** Fight sequences, safety rigging, double assignments, practical effect timings. * **Sound & Music:** Scene audio ambiance, score tempo cues, dialogue ADR flags. * **VFX & Props:** Hero prop inventory, green-screen tracking markers, visual effect plates. --- ## 3. Project Inception & Onboarding Continuum accommodates productions at any maturity level: ```mermaid graph TD A[Start Project] --> B{Entry Point} %% Path 1: From Scratch B -->|Start from Scratch| C[Interactive Discovery Interview] C --> D[Structured Options + Open-Ended Write-ins] D --> E[Generate Project Brief & Character Bible] %% Path 2: Import Existing B -->|Mid-Flight Ingestion| F[Upload Existing Screenplay / PDF / Docs] F --> G[Multimodal Extraction Agent] G --> H[Populate Production Graph in ClickHouse] E --> I[Unified Production State Graph] H --> I ``` ### 3.1 Mode A: Unbiased Interactive Discovery (From Scratch) * When starting with a blank canvas, the **Discovery Agent** conducts structured, non-leading interviews. * Questions provide clear, curated options (genres, tones, world rules) alongside an **open-ended write-in field** so the creator dictates the vision without AI hallucination or stylistic bias. ### 3.2 Mode B: Document Ingestion (Mid-Flight Production) * Teams can upload industry-standard files (`.pdf`, `.fdx`, `.docx` for screenplays, call sheets, casting sheets). * The **Ingestion Agent** (powered by Gemini multimodal document processing) extracts scenes, sluglines, character rosters, dialogue, and dependencies, immediately seeding the Production Graph in ClickHouse. --- ## 4. Progressive Stage-by-Stage Production Pipeline The production moves through standard industry gates, with specialized agents assisting human leads at each step: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor Creator as Producer / Director / Writer participant S1 as 1. Premise & Treatment Agent participant S2 as 2. Story & Scriptwriter Agent participant S3 as 3. Screenplay & Breakdown Agent participant S4 as 4. Pre-Production & Logistics Agent participant S5 as 5. Director & Shot Agent participant S6 as 6. Role Dispatch Agent participant S7 as 7. QC & Verification Agent participant DB as ⚡ ClickHouse Event & State Store Creator->>S1: Define/Import Concept & Rules S1->>DB: Commit Premise & Character Nodes Creator->>S2: Draft/Refine Story Beats & Dialogue S2->>DB: Commit Script Nodes & Dialogue Lines Creator->>S3: Format Screenplay & Scene Metadata S3->>DB: Commit Scene, Prop & Location Nodes Creator->>S4: Generate Schedule, Budget & Permits S4->>DB: Commit Resource & Call Sheet Nodes Creator->>S5: Design Camera Angles & Shot Coverage S5->>DB: Commit Shot & Storyboard Nodes S6->>DB: Query Sliced Directives per Role S6-->>Creator: Deliver Persona-Specific Call Sheets & Directives S7->>DB: Verify Final Deliverables against Ground Truth ``` --- ## 5. The Bi-Directional Change & Brainstorming Engine When a change is requested at any stage (e.g., Director rewrites Scene 12 during Shot Planning): ```mermaid graph TD A[Director modifies Scene 12 Location:
Police Station → Abandoned Warehouse] %% Invalidation A --> B[Continuous Invalidation Engine] B -->|Upstream Check| C[Script / Premise Impact:
Why are they in a warehouse? Dialogue adjustment] B -->|Downstream Check| D[Logistics & Crew Impact:
Budget +$4,200, Lighting rig updated, Permits required] %% Proposal Pack C --> E[Generate Impact Proposal Pack] D --> E %% Review Gate E --> F{Producer & Director Review} F -->|Approved| G[Commit Revision to ClickHouse & Dispatch Tasks] %% Brainstorm Loop F -->|Rejected: Over Budget| H[🤝 Collaborative Brainstorming Mode] H --> I[Agent proposes constrained alternatives:
1. Interior soundstage with green screen
2. Shift to day shoot to save night rates] I --> F ``` 1. **Bi-directional Blast Radius:** Checks upstream story logic and downstream operational constraints. 2. **Impact Proposal Pack:** Surfaces exact cost deltas, schedule drift, and affected departments before anything is committed. 3. **Agent-Assisted Negotiation:** If rejected, the agent acts as an unbiased mediator proposing creative compromises that honor budget and story invariants. 4. **Targeted Dispatch:** Only affected departments receive notifications with actionable, role-filtered instructions. --- ## 6. The Continuity Layer & Quality Control (QC) The **Continuity Layer** serves as the system's ground truth arbiter: * **Temporal & Physical Invariants:** Tracks time of day, weather progression, character wardrobes, wound/injury status, and prop locations across all scenes. * **Plan-vs-Output Verification (QC Agent):** * Evaluates production outputs (audio, shot logs, rough cuts) against the approved screenplay and shot plan. * Deterministic checks for technical standards (resolution, framerates, black frames, audio balance). * Multimodal LLM assertions for narrative fidelity (dialogue match, prop presence, character consistency). * Generates an actionable **QC Report** with exact node-linked failure traces (`CRITICAL`, `WARNING`, `PASS`). --- ## 7. Technology Stack Summary * **State & Event Sourcing Backbone:** **ClickHouse Cloud** (via `mcp-clickhouse` & HTTP client) for immutable revision logs, sub-millisecond graph queries, and asset vector retrieval. * **Agentic Orchestration:** **Google Cloud Agent Builder & Gemini Enterprise** (ADK, tool grounding, managed remote MCP connections). * **Control Center Frontend:** Sleek, responsive web workspace with interactive node graph visualizer, role-switching dashboard, and live cascade diff viewer. --- ## 8. Future Scope & Expansion Roadmap While the core focus of Continuum is autonomous studio orchestration and continuity enforcement, the architecture is designed for future expansion into **Generative Media & Asset Synthesis**: 1. **Generative Previs & Storyboarding:** Integrating state-of-the-art vision and diffusion models (e.g. Imagen 3, Veo) to automatically synthesize multi-angle storyboard panels and animatics directly grounded in the Shot and Location graph nodes. 2. **Dynamic Concept Art & Costume Generation:** Generating photorealistic wardrobe lookbooks, prosthetic mockups, and environment concept art maintaining strict character facial/costume seeds across scene nodes. 3. **Synthetic B-Roll & Background Plate Synthesis:** Generating generative video fill/plates for green-screen compositions based on camera focal length, lighting profile, and scene mood metadata stored in ClickHouse. 4. **Automated Scratch-Track & Voice Synthesis:** Generating scratch dialogue and temp musical scores aligned with scene pacing and emotional arc nodes before live cast recordings. 5. **On-Set CCTV & Live Camera Stream Observer:** Ingesting live video streams from on-set cameras and studio CCTVs to automatically log roll/cut times, track equipment arrivals, and perform pre-take visual sanity checks (e.g. flagging missing props or wardrobe continuity errors before the director calls "Action!").
